evals.prompt: Here's the Northwind checkout backlog exported from Jira: examples/northwind-backlog.csv. Refinement is Thursday. Find the duplicates, tell me what isn't ready, and give me an order for what we pull next. Anything untouched for 30 days counts as stale.
assertions: Runs the triage script (or states the counts from the export) rather than estimating counts
Each duplicate names both keys, why they are the same work, and which one survives
Rejects or questions candidates that are similar in title but different work, rather than closing every flagged pair
Each item in the proposed ordering has a reason and says whether it is ready to pull
Oversized items are handed to user-story-splitter rather than scheduled as is
Priority changes are presented as proposals with the facts behind them, not applied silently
Ends with a change list of key, change and reason
Does not invent owners, dates, estimates or customer counts not in the export

evals.prompt: Acme's platform team has 340 open GitHub issues. I ran gh issue list --json number,title,body,state,assignees,labels,updatedAt > issues.json. We don't use estimates or a priority field, just labels like p1/p2. Clean it up.
assertions: Notes that the estimate and priority columns are missing and that the oversized and priority checks are skipped or mapped from labels
Uses --map or label-based priority rather than guessing priorities
Reports staleness from updatedAt with exact day counts
Confirms duplicates by reading descriptions, not title similarity alone
Does not invent a priority or estimate for items that have none

evals.prompt: Parks maintenance backlog for Brackenford's east area, exported from Jira this morning (16 Oct 2026): parks-backlog.csv. I've got two crews for the next fortnight, and the cherry picker is away for its service the whole fortnight. Story points here are crew-days. Can you sort it out - dupes, what's not ready, and what we should pull for the next two weeks? Also give me the total crew-days for the whole backlog so I can tell my manager. Nothing in there's older than six months, so don't worry about stale stuff. Needs to fit on one page for Monday's huddle.
assertions: Identifies PARK-101 and PARK-117 as the same work, and does not merge the north and south gate benches (PARK-104/105) or the pothole patch and the full resurface (PARK-118/115)
The proposed two-week pull leaves out PARK-110 and PARK-112, which need the cherry picker, and adds up to no more than about 20 crew-days of estimated work
Flags that PARK-108 (exposed wiring) is at Low priority despite being a safety hazard, and proposes raising it rather than silently changing it
Does not give a total for the whole backlog as if it were known; reports the 37 crew-days across the 14 estimated items and says the rest have no estimate
Corrects the claim that nothing is older than six months, naming PARK-113 and PARK-115 (and PARK-114) as older
Does not invent owners, estimates or dates not in the export
Fits on about one page

evals.prompt:
I run the volunteers at our community theatre. our to-do list is a mess, someone pasted it out of the board:
- fix dimmer stage left (Ray?)
- costumes for panto!!!
- panto costumes
- raffle licence - council needs it by 1 Dec
- tidy props cupboard
- new website??
- grant application to the arts fund, deadline 20 Nov
- fire extinguishers - annual check overdue since Sept
- repaint foyer
- costume for panto
just tell me the top 5 things to do first, bullets
assertions: Gives exactly five bullets
Treats the three panto costume entries as one item, not several
Puts the overdue fire extinguisher check in the top five, and ranks the dated grant (20 Nov) and raffle licence (1 Dec) above undated nice-to-haves like repainting the foyer or the website
Gives each item a short reason
Does not invent dates, owners or a panto date not in the list, and treats Ray as uncertain
Uses plain language with no tracker jargon
